text:
Marathon Petroleum shares fell 3% today, pulling back after a sharp three-day rally that had pushed the stock up nearly $25 from last week's low. The decline coincides with news of escalating Iran-U.S. military tensions in the Middle East—a third American aircraft carrier arrived in the Gulf and a tanker was struck in the Hormuz Strait—which typically creates uncertainty about oil supplies and shipping routes. Though crude prices remain relatively stable (U.S. oil at $89.62/barrel), geopolitical risk in a key chokepoint for global oil can spook investors and energy stocks even when prices haven't yet moved.

The broader context shows refineries are running at a healthy 95.2% capacity with solid fuel inventories across gasoline, diesel, and heating oil, so the company's operational picture hasn't deteriorated. The pullback may simply reflect profit-taking after the stock's rapid gain over three days, combined with the reminder that Middle East tensions are a persistent tail risk for energy companies.
